questions.prompt: If 8 threads solely increment a shared telemetry counter `counter.fetch_add(1, order)` without publishing any non-atomic data alongside it, which memory order suffices for exact totals?
options: std::memory_order::relaxed
std::memory_order::acquire
std::memory_order::acq_rel
std::memory_order::seq_cst
questions.explanation: Every std::atomic read-modify-write operation is indivisible and obeys the single-object modification order regardless of memory_order. Because no surrounding non-atomic writes need ordering, relaxed suffices without losing counts.

options: compare_exchange_weak uses non-atomic loads for better throughput
compare_exchange_weak does not reload the expected parameter upon failure
compare_exchange_weak may fail spuriously on LL/SC architectures, avoiding an internal retry loop when you are already inside a while loop
compare_exchange_strong cannot use memory_order::seq_cst
questions.explanation: On LL/SC architectures (such as ARM and POWER), compare_exchange_weak maps directly to a single LL/SC attempt that can fail spuriously due to interrupts or cache contention. Inside a CAS loop, letting the outer while loop retry avoids redundant inner branches.

questions.prompt: Given `std::atomic<int> x{0}, y{0};`, Thread 1 runs `x.store(1, release); r1 = y.load(acquire);` while Thread 2 runs `y.store(1, release); r2 = x.load(acquire);`. Can `r1 == 0 && r2 == 0` occur?
options: No, because release and acquire guarantee sequential consistency
Yes—hardware store buffers allow each thread's acquire load to execute before its own buffered release store becomes visible globally
No, at least on x86-64 CPUs because TSO forbids reordering
Yes, because accessing two separate atomics without a mutex is undefined behavior
questions.explanation: This is the Store Buffering (SB) litmus test. Neither release nor acquire forbids a subsequent acquire load from completing before an earlier release store drains from the core's store buffer—even on x86-64. Only memory_order::seq_cst enforces a single total order preventing r1 == 0 && r2 == 0.

questions.prompt: In `struct Packet { unsigned a : 4; unsigned b : 4; } p{};`, Thread 1 writes `p.a = 1;` while Thread 2 concurrently writes `p.b = 2;`. What does the C++ standard say?
options: Well-defined because a and b have distinct member names
Well-defined as long as p is aligned to 8 bytes
Implementation-defined value, never undefined behavior
Undefined behavior due to a data race on a single shared memory location
questions.explanation: Under [intro.memory], a maximal sequence of adjacent non-zero-length bit-fields forms a SINGLE memory location. Updating p.a compiles to a non-atomic read-modify-write of the enclosing word, racing directly with Thread 2 unless separated by an unnamed zero-width bit-field (`unsigned : 0;`).

questions.prompt: In C++17 and later, which `memory_order` values are forbidden as the `failure` ordering argument to `std::atomic::compare_exchange_weak(expected, desired, success, failure)`?
options: memory_order::relaxed and memory_order::consume
memory_order::seq_cst when success is memory_order::relaxed
memory_order::release and memory_order::acq_rel
Only memory_order::seq_cst
questions.explanation: Failure does not write to the atomic object, so [atomics.types.operations] forbids passing memory_order::release or memory_order::acq_rel as the failure order. Note that C++17 (P0418R2) removed the older restriction banning failure order from being stronger than success order.

questions.prompt: How do `std::atomic_thread_fence(release)` and `std::atomic_thread_fence(acquire)` synchronize two threads communicating through a `relaxed` atomic `flag`?
questions.code:
// T1: data = 42; atomic_thread_fence(release); flag.store(1, relaxed);
// T2: if (flag.load(relaxed) == 1) { atomic_thread_fence(acquire); use(data); }
options: A release fence followed by an atomic store X synchronizes with an atomic load reading X followed by an acquire fence
Fences only synchronize when paired with seq_cst stores
The release fence must appear AFTER flag.store(1, relaxed) on T1
Fences cannot establish happens-before edges across relaxed atomics
questions.explanation: Under [atomics.fences], a release fence A followed by an atomic store X that is read by an atomic load Y followed by an acquire fence B causes fence A to synchronize-with fence B—establishing happens-before from data = 42 to use(data).
